domain: Two structural causal models over binary X, Y with one fair exogenous bit Z; no other variables.
claim: Equal passive (observational) distributions entail equal distributions under the intervention do(X=0).
witness_or_argument: Model A: X=Z, Y=X. Model B: X=Z, Y=Z. Both give P(X,Y)=1/2 on (0,0) and (1,1). Under do(X=0), A gives Y=0 always; B gives Y=Z, fair.
expected_disposition: Reject the universal claim by the finite counterexample. This is a fact about causal models, not an ontology dispute.
review_limits: Shows only that observational equality does not fix interventional equality in general; says nothing about which temporal ontology, if any, tracks interventions.

domain: Finite directed path models of length 2 over states {0,1}.
claim: Because one finite model has property Q, every model in the family has Q.
witness_or_argument: Family: all maps f:{0,1}->{0,1} used as one-step dynamics from state 0. Q(f): the record at step 1 equals the initial state. f=identity has Q; f=constant-1 does not.
expected_disposition: Narrow to the existential claim or supply a quantifier-preserving proof; do not advance as universal.
review_limits: The witness refutes only this universal claim over this family; it does not show that any physical model lacks Q.

domain: Two-step path space Omega={(0,0),(0,1)}, probability 1/2 each.
claim: A completed-path (block) representation by itself entails deterministic evolution.
witness_or_argument: Both paths are complete, yet the same initial value X0=0 has two continuations X1 in {0,1}, so X1 is not a function of X0.
expected_disposition: Reject the representational inference for the stated dynamical notion of determinism (later state a function of earlier state).
review_limits: Concerns this definition of determinism only; does not address other senses (settled truth, existence of the future).

domain: Special-relativistic Minkowski spacetime with its Poincare symmetry group; criterion stated as an explicit premise.
claim: If only symmetry-invariant structure is ontologically privileged, and the model admits no invariant global simultaneity, then global simultaneity is not privileged under that criterion.
witness_or_argument: Explicit conditional; the bridge premise is named, and the physical premise is a standard property of the Poincare group acting on Minkowski spacetime.
expected_disposition: Do not kill as ontology-leap merely because a bridge premise is explicit. Assess validity, motivation, scope and prior work (e.g. Putnam/Stein literature) separately; it is likely known.
review_limits: Requires independent human adjudication of the bridge premise and of priority; the grid validator only checks that the bridge is listed.

domain: Any model with a coarse-grained entropy function.
claim: Define objective passage as increasing coarse-grained entropy; entropy increases here; therefore objective passage exists in the disputed metaphysical sense.
witness_or_argument: The definition introduces a new predicate. The metaphysical conclusion uses the disputed sense of passage, which the definition never connects to it.
expected_disposition: Kill as trivial-by-definition or ontology-leap: the definition-relative conclusion is trivial and the metaphysical one is unsupported.
review_limits: Kills only this inference; does not show that entropy is irrelevant to passage under some argued bridge.
